title: Dominic and the Room
premise: Ivo Dunmore, a pest controller with a talent for things that aren't pests, is hired to clear a house where the infestation leaves fingerprints. He installs sleep recorders to monitor the family, and the tapes reveal a second voice answering questions no one asked aloud. The voice belongs to something taken from the house in 1974 — a child, or what was left of one — and it wants Ivo, who once survived a similar room as a boy, to return what was stolen: its name and its bones, buried beneath the neighbor's extension. As the entity's power grows by feeding on the household's sleep, Ivo must choose between keeping his found family safe and giving the thing exactly what it asks for; in the end he digs up the bones, speaks the name, and lets the room take him instead of the child who lives there now.
about_author: Jude Voss is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent eleven years crawling through other people's basements and never quite got over it. They write horror about houses that remember, and live with two cats who refuse to enter one particular closet.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A routine job at the Halloway house turns strange when he finds small handprints on the inside of a sealed wall cavity. He takes the contract anyway because rent is due. Emotional beat: professional detachment beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He maps the house obsessively — eleven doors, twelve hinges' worth of frames. The youngest Halloway, six-year-old Wren, tells him the extra door only opens when everyone's asleep. Beat: dread establishing itself through domestic detail.

chapters.title: The Recorder
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He rigs audio recorders in each bedroom, telling himself it's standard monitoring. First night captures nothing but breathing — until 3:14 a.m., when every recorder picks up the same slow exhale. Beat: the first undeniable evidence.

chapters.title: Second Voice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, intercut with tape transcripts. The recordings capture a second voice answering questions — patient, childlike, wrong. It knows Ivo's childhood nickname, which no living person uses. Beat: the horror becomes personal.

chapters.title: What Ivo Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, young Ivo's POV, 1989. A rented room during his mother's worst year, a presence that traded safety for small obediences, and how nine-year-old Ivo walked out alive while another kid didn't. Beat: guilt revealed as engine of the story.

chapters.title: The Halloways
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs: Mara Halloway, exhausted single mother, and her teenage son Dev. Sleep deprivation frays them; Dev starts sleepwalking toward the sealed wall. Ivo realizes the house isn't haunting them — it's feeding. Beat: found-family bonds forming under pressure.

Ivo's POV at the county archive. He finds records: a child named Ellis Vane vanished from the property in 1974, case closed as a runaway. The previous owner's diary describes 'returning what we took.' Beat: the mystery acquires a body count and a deadline.

chapters.title: The Neighbor's Extension
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ground-penetrating radar on the neighboring lot shows a disturbance beneath a sunroom built in 1975. The voice on the tapes grows stronger each night, and Wren begins speaking in unison with it. Beat: rising urgency.

chapters.title: Permission
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Ivo tells her the truth; she nearly throws him out, then plays the tape of the voice using Wren's laughter. She agrees to help dig. Beat: alliance forged in terror, trust established.

chapters.title: The Dig
chapters.summary: Ivo and Dev's POV, night excavation. Beneath the sunroom slab: a small tin box containing children's bones and a hand-lettered name tag reading ELLIS. The moment they touch it, every door in both houses opens at once. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: What Came Back
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. With the bones disturbed, the entity stops whispering and starts arriving — cold rooms, wet footprints, Wren reciting addresses from 1974. Ivo understands returning the bones isn't enough; the thing wants acknowledgment, a witness. Beat: escalation into open haunting.

chapters.title: The Room
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following the footprints, he finds the sealed cavity now opens onto a room that shouldn't fit inside the house — wallpaper from his childhood rental, his mother's chair. The entity has been building a trap out of his memory. Beat: past and present collapse together.

chapters.title: Dev Taken
chapters.summary: Dev's POV, then Mara's. Dev sleepwalks into the room and doesn't come out; the door seals flush with the wall. On the recorder, Dev's voice answers questions in the second voice's cadence. Beat: devastating midpoint loss.

chapters.title: Bargaining
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV at the sealed wall. He negotiates aloud: himself for Dev. The voice agrees but sets terms — the bones returned to the room, the name spoken by someone who knew Ellis, within three nights. Beat: terrible hope with strings attached.

chapters.title: Ellis Vane
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV researching Ellis. He tracks down Ellis's sister, now seventy, in a care home. Her account reframes everything: Ellis wasn't taken by the house — the 1974 owners fed the room deliberately, and Ellis's death bound it here. Beat: the true villain revealed as human greed.

chapters.title: The Sister
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Ivo and elderly June Vane. June gives Ivo Ellis's real full name — the one erased from all records — and a locket with a lock of hair. She asks him to tell Ellis she never stopped looking. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Second Night
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The household holds vigil; the entity tests them with illusions — Dev's voice begging, Wren's doppelganger in the hallway. Mara holds the line by refusing to answer any voice she can't touch. Beat: resilience against manipulation.

chapters.title: Third Night
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Carrying the box and the locket, Ivo enters the room. It wears his childhood like skin, offering him the safety he sold his soul wanting at nine years old. He almost stays. Beat: temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: The Name
chapters.summary: Climax, Ivo's POV. In the room's heart he finds Dev frozen mid-sleepwalk and the entity wearing Ellis's face, starving and furious. Ivo speaks the true name, returns the bones and hair, and bears witness to what was done. The room begins to come apart around them. Beat: catharsis through truth-telling.

chapters.title: Exchange
chapters.summary: Climax continued, Ivo's POV. The collapsing room demands its price: a keeper. Ivo puts Dev outside the threshold and steps back in, trading his freedom for the child's — mirroring and redeeming his survival in 1989. Beat: sacrifice as the ultimate cost of survival.

chapters.title: After
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, weeks later. The house is warm, ordinary, doors exactly eleven. Dev remembers nothing; Wren sometimes waves at an empty corner. Mara keeps Ivo's tools in the garage and his recorder running, just in case. Beat: mourning braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: The Lights Stay On
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ivo's POV inside the room-that-isn't. He keeps the lights on and counts the doors — now infinite — and hears, faintly, a second voice that sounds like Ellis, finally at peace, keeping him company. Last line implies he's teaching the room to let people go. Beat: bittersweet resolution, found family enduring across the threshold.
